outcome: No event dated after 26 January 2024 was found that moves the Bost conjecture itself. The Bost-specific results I could date are all from 2007 to 2013, and the in-window items found concern the parent Farrell–Jones conjecture or the Baum–Connes conjecture, so they are discounted for this bullet.
problem_asks: (a) That the Bost assembly map is an isomorphism, i.e. the Bost conjecture as the list states it. The one-line list entry does not name the map. The map used here (equivariant K-homology of E_FIN(G) with l1-type coefficients, mapping to K_*(l1(G))) is taken from the Bost section of the Farrell–Jones Wikipedia article, not from the statement itself. (b) That the Bost conjecture is a specific case of the Farrell–Jones conjecture, as the list's sub-bullet under the Farrell–Jones entry says. Whether the sources support (b) is a finding; see summary. The statement as given leaves open which groups (the sources I read say all countable discrete groups) and which coefficients (trivial in the Farrell–Jones article; C*-algebra coefficients in Paravicini's 2009 papers).

events.what_happened: V. Lafforgue's 2002 Banach KK-theory work on the Baum–Connes conjecture, cited by Paravicini (arXiv:0902.4339, section 2) for the claims that 'the proper case was already settled' there and that the Bost conjecture is 'actually true for proper C*-algebras'. The 2002 paper itself was not located or opened in this pass, so this event rests on one citation. The title is recalled from memory as 'K-theorie bivariante pour les algebres de Banach et conjecture de Baum-Connes' and is unverified.
events.delivers: Per the citation only: the Bost conjecture for proper coefficient algebras. Not verified against the 2002 text.
events.remains: The Bost conjecture for non-proper coefficients and for general groups.
events.time_since_posted: about 24 years; no follow-up examined in this pass
events.direction: Positive partial result, consistent with the conjecture (per the citation).

events.what_happened: Bartels, Echterhoff and Lueck, 'Inheritance of isomorphism conjectures under colimits' (arXiv math/0702460, v1 15 Feb 2007; v2 also on arXiv; later appears as a chapter in an EMS volume, ems.press/books/ecr/60/1190, year not checked). The abstract states that the K-theoretic Farrell–Jones conjecture and 'the Bost Conjecture with coefficients' hold for those groups for which Higson, Lafforgue and Skandalis disproved the Baum–Connes conjecture with coefficients. It also studies inheritance of Baum–Connes, Bost and Farrell–Jones under colimits of groups over directed sets.
events.revisions: v1 15 Feb 2007; a v2 is listed on arXiv; EMS chapter publication year not checked.
events.delivers: For the class of groups where Higson–Lafforgue–Skandalis disproved Baum–Connes with coefficients, the Bost conjecture with coefficients holds (and so does the K-theoretic Farrell–Jones conjecture). Also inheritance of the three isomorphism conjectures under colimits over directed sets, with non-injective structure maps. Restricted to that class and to the coefficient version.
events.remains: The Bost conjecture for all countable discrete groups and for groups outside that class. The abstract states the Bost result for the coefficient version only.
events.time_since_posted: about 19 years; I did not search citing papers for a review, so silence is not established either way
events.direction: Consistent with the Bost conjecture: it holds for a class of groups where Baum–Connes with coefficients fails. It gives no counterexample to Bost.

events.what_happened: Walther Paravicini, 'Induction for Banach algebras, groupoids and KK^ban' (arXiv 0902.4199, v1 24 Feb 2009, only version listed). The paper shows that for two equivalent locally compact Hausdorff groupoids the Bost conjecture with Banach-algebra coefficients holds for one if and only if it holds for the other, and proves functoriality of Lafforgue's KK-theory for Banach algebras and groupoids. Later published in the Journal of K-Theory (per a search result; not opened).
events.delivers: An invariance statement: the Bost conjecture with Banach-algebra coefficients is preserved under equivalence of locally compact Hausdorff groupoids. It settles no particular group.
events.remains: Whether the Bost conjecture holds for any given group; the entire conjecture for groups is untouched.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (per a search result, publication year not checked)

events.direction: Neutral for the conjecture's truth. It is a structural invariance result.

events.what_happened: Walther Paravicini, 'The Bost conjecture, open subgroups and groups acting on trees' (arXiv 0902.4339, v1 25 Feb 2009, only version listed; arXiv listing used). The abstract: the Bost conjecture with C*-algebra coefficients for locally compact Hausdorff groups passes to open subgroups; if a locally compact Hausdorff group acts on a tree, the conjecture holds for the group if and only if it holds for the vertex stabilisers. Later published in the Journal of K-Theory (per a search result). Note: the ar5iv rendering of the same paper carries an internal date of 31 May 2008; the arXiv identifier and listing give February 2009, and I used the listing date.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (25 Feb 2009). The ar5iv copy is dated 31 May 2008 in its text.
events.delivers: For the C*-algebra-coefficient version of the Bost conjecture on locally compact Hausdorff groups: passage to open subgroups, and for groups acting on trees an if-and-only-if reduction to vertex stabilisers. Restricted to that coefficient version and to the stated reductions.
events.remains: The Bost conjecture for general closed subgroups (the paper notes it would pass to closed subgroups if a map psi* were an isomorphism, which it does not establish) and for groups in general.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (per a search result, publication year not checked)

events.direction: Partial reductions, consistent with the conjecture. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: A. J. Berrick, I. Chatterji and G. Mislin, 'From acyclic groups to the Bass conjecture for amenable groups' (arXiv 1004.1941, first submitted 12 Apr 2010). Abstract: 'We prove that the Bost Conjecture on the l1-assembly map for countable discrete groups implies the Bass Conjecture. It follows that all amenable groups satisfy the Bass Conjecture.' The paper's Theorem 1.3, attributed to Lafforgue in a search snippet, asserts the Bost isomorphism for groups with the Haagerup property; I could not read that theorem (see incomplete).
events.revisions: v1 12 Apr 2010; later versions not checked.
events.delivers: A conditional implication: Bost for countable discrete groups implies the l1 Bass conjecture. Per the abstract, amenable groups therefore satisfy the Bass conjecture. The abstract does not itself establish Bost for amenable groups.
events.remains: Bost for all countable discrete groups. The amenable-group consequence concerns the Bass conjecture, not Bost.
events.time_since_posted: about 16 years 6 months; no follow-up examined in this pass
events.direction: Conditional on Bost; neutral on whether Bost holds.

events.what_happened: Walther Paravicini, 'The Bost conjecture and proper Banach algebras', J. Noncommut. Geom. 7 (2013), no. 1, 191–202, DOI 10.4171/JNCG/113. The journal page gives submission on 2 Dec 2010 and publication on 8 Mar 2013. The arXiv version, if any, was not located, so 2 Dec 2010 is the earliest date I could establish and is a journal submission date, not a public posting date.
events.revisions: Date is the journal submission date. Arxiv posting not located.
events.delivers: For proper Banach-algebra coefficients, the Bost assembly map is split surjective, and the right-hand side of the conjecture does not depend on the choice of unconditional completion. Surjectivity only; the isomorphism is not established by this result.
events.remains: Injectivity, and so the isomorphism, for proper Banach-algebra coefficients; and the Bost conjecture for non-proper coefficients and for general groups.

The paper proves the Farrell–Jones conjecture with coefficients in left-exact infinity-categories for finitely F-amenable groups and Dress–Farrell–Hsiang–Jones groups. It is a Farrell–Jones paper, not a Bost paper. The date recorded is an upper bound: José Francisco Reis's arXiv:2211.15523 (Nov 2022, from a search snippet) describes the result as already proved. The Bunke–Kasprowski–Winges preprint and its posting date were not located, and the full text was not readable.

Ann. 395:89 (2026) per search results). The abstract proves the fibred Farrell–Jones conjecture in A-, K- and L-theory for a large class of suspensions of relatively hyperbolic groups, and for all suspensions of one-ended hyperbolic groups. It is a Farrell–Jones paper and does not mention Bost in the abstract or in the part of the text I read.

events.what_happened: Jianguo Zhang, arXiv 2506.18446: v1 posted 23 Jun 2025 (title per a search result: 'The Baum–Connes conjecture for extensions revisited'); v2 posted 23 Aug 2025 with the title 'A localization algebra approach to the Baum–Connes conjecture for extensions'. The paper concerns the Baum–Connes conjecture with coefficients, not Bost. The arXiv comments say v1 'there exists an essential mistake in Theorem 3.13', identified by Ralf Meyer and Shintaro Nishikawa; v2 strengthened that theorem's conditions. The v2 abstract says it proves 'this known result' (Baum–Connes for an extension, given it holds for the quotient and for the preimages of finite subgroups) using a localization algebra approach.

The note gives a counterexample showing that the assumptions Chabert and Echterhoff impose in their permanence result for Baum–Connes under group extensions cannot be simplified, which refutes Zhang's proposed simplification (per the search summary of the journal version, which I did not open). It concerns Baum–Connes with coefficients, not Bost. The abstract and metadata do not mention Bost.

disputes.summary: Zhang's 2025 claim that Baum–Connes with coefficients passes to an extension from the normal subgroup and the quotient alone was refuted by Ralf Meyer's counterexample. Zhang's v1 had an essential mistake in Theorem 3.13, identified by Meyer and Nishikawa; v2 strengthened that theorem's conditions. This concerns Baum–Connes, not Bost.

summary: No Bost-specific event dated inside the window was found. The Bost results I could date are: Bartels–Echterhoff–Lueck (arXiv Feb 2007), Bost with coefficients for groups where Baum–Connes with coefficients fails; Paravicini (arXiv Feb 2009 ×2), invariance under groupoid equivalence and, for the C*-coefficient version, passage to open subgroups and an if-and-only-if reduction for groups acting on trees; Berrick–Chatterji–Mislin (arXiv Apr 2010), Bost implies the l1 Bass conjecture; and Paravicini (journal submission Dec 2010, published 2013), surjectivity of the Bost assembly map for proper Banach-algebra coefficients. Each is partial and none establishes the isomorphism for all groups. The in-window items I found are neighbouring: Farrell–Jones (Lueck's 2025 survey; Andrew–Guerch–Hughes, posted Nov 2023 with v2 in 2026; Bunke–Kasprowski–Winges, 2026 journal) and Baum–Connes (Zhang 2025 and Meyer's Aug 2025 counterexample; Guo–Wang–Yao Jan 2026). None of these mentions Bost in the text I could read. Close calls: (1) The list calls Bost 'a specific case of the Farrell–Jones conjecture', and the Farrell–Jones article's Bost section describes it as the l1 analogue of Baum–Connes. The sources I read treat the two as parallel isomorphism conjectures (Bartels–Echterhoff–Lueck 2007), and I found no source that reduces Bost to Farrell–Jones, so the list's framing is unverified. The Farrell–Jones article states that no counterexamples to Farrell–Jones are known. (2) Which version of Bost: the 2009 and 2013 Paravicini results concern C*-algebra or Banach-algebra coefficients on locally compact groups, while the list and the Farrell–Jones article state the discrete-group version with trivial coefficients. The two may not be the same quantity. (3) Dates: Paravicini 2009 open-subgroups uses the arXiv listing (25 Feb 2009); the ar5iv copy carries an internal date of 31 May 2008. The 2013 Banach-algebra paper's arXiv posting was not located, so its date is the journal submission date. (4) Lafforgue's 2002 result is known here only through Paravicini's citation. Search summaries attributed to Liao–Yu (arXiv 1708.01982) and to the 2019 survey (Gomez Aparicio–Julg–Valette, arXiv 1905.10081) claims that Bost holds for large classes of groups, including lattices; the abstract I read for Liao–Yu does not mention Bost, and the 2019 survey's Bost section was not reached, so those claims are unverified. On AI: no source found links an AI system to the Bost conjecture, to Farrell–Jones for these groups, or to Baum–Connes in these items. The AI-related items found (arXiv 2604.03789, a Lean-based pipeline; arXiv 2607.20525 and 2608.29595, GPT-based counterexample work; arXiv 2608.11941, OEIS Open; arXiv 2608.12561, a Borsuk example credited to ChatGPT) concern other problems and do not mention Bost, Baum–Connes or Farrell–Jones. The Erdős-problems AI tracker on GitHub was opened and has no entry on these topics. The search tool indexes arXiv only partially, so absence in search results is weak evidence.
competing_reading: The strongest case for counting in-window work as Bost progress is the list's own framing: if Bost is a specific case of Farrell–Jones, then Farrell–Jones results on new classes of groups (Andrew–Guerch–Hughes, Bunke–Kasprowski–Winges, Lueck's survey) would give the Bost conjecture for those groups, and that would be a move inside the window. The strongest case against counting the 2007–2013 Bost results as settling anything is that each is a partial reduction, invariance, or surjectivity statement for a coefficient version, not the isomorphism itself. A reader who takes the 2009 C*-coefficient results as covering the list's discrete-group, trivial-coefficient statement would count more than I have.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A source that states the Bost conjecture as a special case of the Farrell–Jones conjecture, with the precise reduction. (2) The full text of Lueck's 2025 survey (arXiv 2507.11337, sections 7.5–11 and references) and of Bunke–Kasprowski–Winges, checked for any Bost statement. (3) The Bost sections of Gomez Aparicio–Julg–Valette (arXiv 1905.10081, section 6.1.2 onward), Lafforgue's 2002 paper, and Berrick–Chatterji–Mislin's Theorem 1.3, for the exact status of Bost for amenable, hyperbolic and lattice groups. (4) A listing of Bost-titled or Bost-section papers on arXiv math.KT and math.OA from 2024 onward, which web search cannot provide. (5) Whether the Lean formal-conjectures repository contains a Bost or Farrell–Jones statement.
